## Analysis population

Our goal is to investigate the diagnostic ability of miRNAs in `r text_disease`. In this analysis we are looking at `r text_intro`.

*   **Patient population:** Patients from the BestAgeing study ($n_{total}=$ `r nrow(data01)`)
*   **Disease:** `r text_disease` ($n_{disease}=$ `r length(eval(as.symbol(disease_vector)))`) vs controls ($n_{control}=$ `r length(control_ids)`)
*   **Input:** `r no.mirnas` miRNAs adjusted for `age` and `sex`
*   **Output:** Probability of being diagnosed with `r text_disease`
*   **Algorithms:**
    + Logistic Regression with Elastic net regularization 
    + KNN
    + Random Forest
    + Support Vector Machine
    + Neural Net


\clearpage

# Model

## Screening many models

A good strategy is to spend some initial effort trying a variety of modeling approaches, determine what works best, then invest additional time tweaking/ optimizing a small set of models. 
\
We are going to explore the performance of the following classification algorithms: 

- KNN
- Penalized logistic regression
- Random forest
- XGBoost
- Support Vector Machines
- Neural net

## Training Data

### Initial Split

We can start by splitting our data into training and testing sets. We also remove the "work-up" columns because decision should be made before workup can be done. 

```{r split-data}
set.seed(123)

if (params$analysis == "selected") {
  # only 114 mirnas in analysis
  modeldat <- eval(as.symbol(selected_mirna_dat)) 
  } else{
    # full analysis with all mirnas
    modeldat <- data01
}

# make control first factor for all analyses ;)
modeldat <- modeldat %>% 
  mutate(disease = factor(disease, levels = c("control", params$disease)))

dat_split <- rsample::initial_split(modeldat, strata = disease)
dat_train <- training(dat_split)
dat_test <- testing(dat_split)

folds <- 
  vfold_cv(dat_train, strata = disease, v = 5)
```

### Preprocessing Recipe

Next we build recipes for data preprocessing. Some models (notably neural networks, K-NN, and SVM) require predictors that have been centered and scaled. For other models, a traditional response surface design model expansion (i.e., quadratic and two-way interactions) is a good idea. 

```{r recipe}
normalized_rec <- 
  recipe(disease ~ ., data = dat_train) %>%
  ### https://recipes.tidymodels.org/articles/Ordering.html
  #  To make sure we don’t get any unexpected results, it’s best to use 
  #  the following ordering of high-level transformations:
  #     Skewness Transformations - step_YeoJohnson()
  #     Centering, Scaling, or Normalization on Numeric Predictors
  #     Dummy Variables for Categorical Data
  update_role(pat_id, new_role="ID") %>% 
  step_zv(all_predictors()) %>%  
  step_impute_mean(all_numeric_predictors()) %>% 
  step_impute_mode(all_nominal_predictors(), -disease) %>% 
  step_corr(all_numeric_predictors(), threshold = 0.9) %>% 
  step_YeoJohnson() %>% 
  step_normalize(all_numeric_predictors()) %>%  
  step_dummy(all_nominal_predictors(),-disease)

poly_rec <- 
  recipe(disease ~ ., data = dat_train) %>%
  update_role(pat_id, new_role="ID") %>% 
  step_zv(all_predictors()) %>%  
  step_impute_mean(all_numeric_predictors()) %>% 
  step_impute_mode(all_nominal_predictors(), -disease) %>% 
  step_corr(all_numeric_predictors(), threshold = 0.9) %>% 
  step_normalize(all_numeric_predictors()) %>%  
  step_poly(all_numeric_predictors()) %>% 
  step_dummy(all_nominal_predictors(),-disease) #%>% 
  #step_interact( ~all_predictors():all_predictors())

simple_rec <- 
  recipe(disease ~ ., data = dat_train) %>%
  update_role(pat_id, new_role="ID") %>% 
  # ZERO VARIANCE
  step_zv(all_predictors()) %>%  
  # IMPUTE
  step_impute_mean(all_numeric_predictors()) %>% 
  step_impute_mode(all_nominal_predictors(), -disease) %>% 
  # DECORRELATE
  step_corr(all_numeric_predictors(), threshold = 0.9) %>% 
  step_dummy(all_nominal_predictors(),-disease)
```

The above mentioned preprocessing specifications can be recycled across models and can be used on the test data afterwards easily. 

### Define model engines and set the tuning specifications

```{r parsnip-specs}
#parsnip::set_dependency("kknn", "glmnet", "ranger", "naivebayes") #, "kernlab", "xgboost", "nnet")

nearest_neighbor_kknn_spec <-
  nearest_neighbor(neighbors = tune(), weight_func = tune(), 
                   dist_power = tune()) %>%
  set_engine('kknn') %>%
  set_mode('classification')

logistic_reg_glmnet_spec <-
  logistic_reg(penalty = tune(), mixture = tune()) %>%
  set_mode("classification") %>% 
  set_engine('glmnet')

rand_forest_ranger_spec <-
  rand_forest(mtry = tune(), min_n = tune()) %>%
  set_engine('ranger') %>%
  set_mode('classification')

library(discrim)
naive_Bayes_naivebayes_spec <-
  naive_Bayes(smoothness = tune(), Laplace = tune()) %>%
  set_engine('naivebayes') %>% 
  set_mode('classification')

svm_linear_kernlab_spec <-
  svm_linear(cost = tune(), margin = tune()) %>%
  set_engine('kernlab') %>%
  set_mode('classification')

svm_poly_kernlab_spec <-
  svm_poly(cost = tune(), degree = tune(), 
           scale_factor = tune(), margin = tune()) %>%
  set_engine('kernlab') %>%
  set_mode('classification')

svm_rbf_kernlab_spec <-
  svm_rbf(cost = tune(), rbf_sigma = tune(), margin = tune()) %>%
  set_engine('kernlab') %>%
  set_mode('classification')

boost_tree_xgboost_spec <-  # https://parsnip.tidymodels.org/reference/details_boost_tree_xgboost.html
  boost_tree(trees = tune(), tree_depth = tune(), 
             min_n = tune(),                              ## first three: model complexity
             loss_reduction = tune(), 
             stop_iter = tune(), 
             sample_size = tune(), mtry = tune(),         ## randomness
             learn_rate = tune(),                         ## step size
             ) %>%
  set_engine('xgboost') %>%
  set_mode('classification')

mlp_nnet_spec <-
  mlp(hidden_units = tune(), penalty = tune(), 
      epochs = tune()) %>%
  set_engine('nnet') %>%
  set_mode('classification')
```


### Workflow Set

```{r workflows}
## A
normalized <- 
  workflow_set(   # IDs are generated {name of preproc} + {name of model}
    preproc = list(normalized = normalized_rec),
    models = list(
      KNN = nearest_neighbor_kknn_spec, 
      SVM_radial = svm_rbf_kernlab_spec, 
      SVM_poly = svm_poly_kernlab_spec, 
      SVM_linear = svm_linear_kernlab_spec,
      neural_network = mlp_nnet_spec
    )
  )

## B
simple <- 
  workflow_set(
    preproc = list(simple = simple_rec),
    models = list(
      #naive_bayes = naive_Bayes_naivebayes_spec,    ## ERROR when tuning "Error in pkgs$pkg[[1]] : subscript out of bounds"
      RF = rand_forest_ranger_spec,
      XGB = boost_tree_xgboost_spec
    )
  )

## C
with_features <- 
  workflow_set(
    preproc = list(full_quad = poly_rec),
    models = list(
      logistic_reg = logistic_reg_glmnet_spec,
      KNN = nearest_neighbor_kknn_spec
    )
  )

# normalized %>% extract_workflow(id = "normalized_KNN")

## these objects are tibbles -> row binding does not affect the state of the sets
### result is itself a workflow set
all_workflows <- 
  bind_rows(simple, normalized, with_features) %>% 
  # make workflow IDs a little more simple:
  mutate(wflow_id = gsub("(simple_)|(normalized_)", "", wflow_id))
```

```{r define-grids}
# need to finalize mtry - data dependent (unknown values - how many predictors?)
## data dependent: mtry(), sample_size(), num_terms(), num_comp()
set.seed(123)
if (params$analysis == "selected") {
  # only 114 mirnas in analysis
  grid_RF <- rand_forest_ranger_spec %>%   # 2 hyperparams
    extract_parameter_set_dials() %>% 
    # data dependent
    update(mtry = mtry(range = c(1, ncol(dat_train))) ) %>% 
    grid_latin_hypercube(size=50) 
  } else{
    # full analysis with all mirnas: limit `mtry()`
  grid_RF <- rand_forest_ranger_spec %>% 
      extract_parameter_set_dials() %>% 
      # data dependent
      update(mtry = mtry(range = c(1, ncol(dat_train)/2)) ) %>%  # not using all features
      grid_latin_hypercube(size=50) 
}

if (params$analysis == "selected") {
  # only 114 mirnas in analysis
  grid_XGB <- boost_tree_xgboost_spec %>%   # 2 hyperparams
    extract_parameter_set_dials() %>% 
    # data dependent
    update(mtry = mtry(range = c(1, ncol(dat_train))) ) %>% 
    grid_latin_hypercube(size=50) 
  } else{
    # full analysis with all mirnas: limit `mtry()`
  grid_XGB <- boost_tree_xgboost_spec %>% 
      extract_parameter_set_dials() %>% 
      # data dependent
      update(mtry = mtry(range = c(1, ncol(dat_train)/2)) ) %>%  # not using all features
      grid_latin_hypercube(size=50) 
}

grid_KNN <- nearest_neighbor_kknn_spec %>%  # 3 hyperparams
  extract_parameter_set_dials() %>%
  grid_latin_hypercube(size=50)

grid_SVM_radial <- svm_rbf_kernlab_spec %>%   # 3 hyperparams
  extract_parameter_set_dials() %>%
  grid_latin_hypercube(size=50)

grid_SVM_poly <- svm_poly_kernlab_spec %>%   # 4 hyperparams
  extract_parameter_set_dials() %>%
  grid_latin_hypercube(size=75)

grid_SVM_linear <- svm_linear_kernlab_spec %>%   # 2 hyperparams
  extract_parameter_set_dials() %>%
  grid_latin_hypercube(size=50)

grid_neural_network <- mlp_nnet_spec %>%   # 3 hyperparams
  extract_parameter_set_dials() %>% 
  grid_latin_hypercube(size=75)

grid_full_quad_logistic_reg <- logistic_reg_glmnet_spec %>%  # 2 hyperparams
  extract_parameter_set_dials() %>% 
  grid_latin_hypercube(size=50)

## supply grid to workflow options
# https://github.com/tidymodels/workflowsets/issues/37
all_workflows <- all_workflows %>% 
  option_add(grid = grid_RF, id = "RF") %>% 
  option_add(grid = grid_XGB, id = "XGB") %>% 
  option_add(grid = grid_KNN, id = "KNN") %>% 
  option_add(grid = grid_SVM_radial, id = "SVM_radial") %>% 
  option_add(grid = grid_SVM_poly, id = "SVM_poly") %>% 
  option_add(grid = grid_SVM_linear, id = "SVM_linear") %>% 
  option_add(grid = grid_neural_network, id = "neural_network") %>% 
  option_add(grid = grid_full_quad_logistic_reg, id = "full_quad_logistic_reg") %>% 
  option_add(grid = grid_KNN, id = "full_quad_KNN")   # same hyperparams
```


### Tuning the models with small grid

```{r tune-grid-workflows}
## outsourced to `scripts/model.R`

# select DISEASE and ANALYSIS from path -> choose last one trained
index <- str_detect(string = list.files(path = "../output/tuning_results"), pattern = text_disease)  & 
  str_detect(list.files(path = "../output/tuning_results"), pattern = str_to_upper(params$analysis)) & 
  str_detect(list.files(path = "../output/tuning_results"), pattern = "tune_grid")

if(index != FALSE) {   # if no models tuned and saved index evaluates to FALSE!
  grid_results <- readRDS(
    dplyr::last(list.files(path = "../output/tuning_results", full.names = TRUE)[index])
    )

  num_grid_models <- nrow(collect_metrics(grid_results, summarize = FALSE))
}
```

What do our `grid_results` look like?

```{r workflow-sets-grid-print}
if(index != FALSE) {
  #grid_results
  grid_results %>% 
    rank_results() %>% 
    filter(.metric == "roc_auc") %>% 
    select(model, .config, roc_auc=mean, rank) -> rankings
  
  top2models_grid <- rankings$model[1:2]
  for (i in 1:length(all_workflows$info)) {
    if (all_workflows$info[[i]]$model == top2models_grid[1]) {
      topmodel1_grid <- all_workflows$wflow_id[i]
    }
    
      if (all_workflows$info[[i]]$model == top2models_grid[2]) {
      topmodel2_grid <- all_workflows$wflow_id[i]
    }
  }
  
  autoplot(
     grid_results,
     rank_metric = "roc_auc",  # <- how to order models
     metric = "roc_auc",       # <- which metric to visualize
     select_best = TRUE     # <- one point per workflow
  ) +
    geom_text(aes(y = mean - 0.05, label = wflow_id), angle = 45, hjust = 1, size =3) +
    lims(y = c(0.6, 1.0)) +
    labs(title="Ranking models",
         subtitle="Grid approach")+
    ylab("ROC-AUC")+
    ggthemes::theme_few()+
    theme(legend.position = "none")
  
  # inspect hyperparameter results for specific model
  autoplot(grid_results, id = topmodel1_grid, metric = "roc_auc")+
    ylab("ROC-AUC")+
    labs(title="Hyperparameter Performance",
         subtitle = stringr::str_to_upper(topmodel1_grid))+
    ggthemes::theme_few()
  
  autoplot(grid_results, id = topmodel2_grid, metric = "roc_auc")+
    ylab("ROC-AUC")+
    labs(title="Hyperparameter Performance - Grid Approach",
         subtitle = stringr::str_to_upper(topmodel2_grid))+
    ggthemes::theme_few()
}
```

```{r workflow-sets-racing-concordance}
matched_results <- 
   rank_results(race_results, select_best = TRUE) %>% 
   select(wflow_id, .metric, race = mean, config_race = .config) %>% 
   inner_join(
      rank_results(grid_results, select_best = TRUE) %>% 
         select(wflow_id, .metric, complete = mean, 
                config_complete = .config, model),
      by = c("wflow_id", ".metric"),
   ) %>%  
   filter(.metric == "roc_auc")

matched_results %>% 
  ggplot(aes(x = complete, y = race)) + 
  geom_abline(lty = 3) + 
  geom_point() + 
  geom_text_repel(aes(label = model)) +
  coord_obs_pred() + 
  labs(x = "Complete Grid ROC-AUC", y = "Racing ROC-AUC") +
  ggthemes::theme_few()
```

### Fit model to training data

There are several combinations that look good. We identify the best combinations based on ROC-AUC, and then update our workflow specification with the numerically best settings, and fit to the training set.

* Top model 1: `r topmodel1_race`
* Top model 2: `r topmodel2_race`

```{r workflow-sets-finalize2}
## TOP MODEL 1
best_results1 <- race_results %>% 
   extract_workflow_set_result(topmodel1_race) %>% 
   select_best(metric = "roc_auc")

test_results1 <-  race_results %>% 
   extract_workflow(topmodel1_race) %>% 
   finalize_workflow(best_results1) %>% 
   last_fit(split = dat_split)

## TOP MODEL 2
best_results2 <- race_results %>% 
   extract_workflow_set_result(topmodel2_race) %>% 
   select_best(metric = "roc_auc")

test_results2 <-  race_results %>% 
   extract_workflow(topmodel2_race) %>% 
   finalize_workflow(best_results2) %>% 
   last_fit(split = dat_split)
```

We look at the Metrics and the Confusion Matrix.

```{r roc-test-check}

ci.auc.text <- paste("AUC CI: ", round(ci.auc[1],2), "-",round(ci.auc[3],2), " DeLong" , sep = "")


predictions <- predictions %>% 
  mutate(.pred_class_youden = ifelse(predictions[[pred_string]] <= youden.threshold, "control", params$disease ),

  ## factor order usually alphabetically! (acs < control)
  mutate(disease = factor(disease, levels=c("control", params$disease))) %>%

  ggplot(aes(1 - specificity, sensitivity)) +
```

## Metrics on Test Set | All models

```{r loop, fig.show="hold", out.width="50%", warning=FALSE}
best_results <- list()  # hyperparams selected
test_results <- list()  # last fit

aucs <- c()
ci.auc.texts <- c()
accuracies <- c()
sensitiv <- c()
specific <- c()
ppv <- c()
npv <- c()
precision <- c()
recall <- c()
f1 <- c()

conf_mat_list <- list()
predictions_loop <- list()
caret_conf_mat <- list()

coefficients_loop <- list()


for (i in seq_along(1:nrow(race_results)) ) {
  ## retrieve ID
  wflow_id <- race_results[[1]][i]
  # select best hyperparams
  best_results[[i]] <- 
     race_results %>% 
     extract_workflow_set_result(wflow_id) %>% 
     select_best(metric = "roc_auc")
  # fit to training data, and calculate on test data
  test_results[[i]] <- 
     race_results %>% 
     extract_workflow(wflow_id) %>% 
     finalize_workflow(best_results[[i]]) %>% 
     last_fit(split = dat_split)
  
  ## 1) STORE TEST_SET_RESULTS -----------
  testresults_save <- paste0(format(params$date, "%Y%m%d"),  "_TEST_RESULTS_", wflow_id, "_", "DISEASE_",
                      params$disease,"_ANALYSIS_", params$analysis)
  filename.testresults <- paste0("../output/test_set_results/", testresults_save, ".rds")
  saveRDS(test_results[[i]], file = filename.testresults)
  
  ## 2) STORE MODEL ### ------------------
  last_fit_metrics <- collect_metrics(test_results[[i]])
  # extract model
  last_fit_model <- extract_workflow(test_results[[i]])

  ## VETIVER MODEL DEPLOYMENT
  modelname <- paste0(format(params$date, "%Y%m%d"),  "_MODEL_", wflow_id, "_", "DISEASE_",
                      params$disease,"_ANALYSIS_", params$analysis)
  filename.model.vetiver <- paste0("../output/models/vetiver/", modelname, ".rds")
  filename.model.tidymodels <- paste0("../output/models/tidymodels/", modelname, ".rds")
  v <- vetiver_model(
    model = last_fit_model, 
    model_name = modelname, 
    metadata = list(metrics = last_fit_metrics %>% select(-.config))
  )
  saveRDS(v, file = filename.model.vetiver)
  saveRDS(last_fit_model, file = filename.model.tidymodels)
  ###
  
  aucs <- append(aucs, collect_metrics(test_results[[i]])[[3]][2])
  accuracies <- append(accuracies, collect_metrics(test_results[[i]])[[3]][1])
  
  predictions_loop[[i]] <- test_results[[i]] %>%
    collect_predictions() 
  
  ### --> get optimal threshold (YOUDEN INDEX) & extract CI AUC
  my_roc <- pROC::roc(predictions_loop[[i]]$disease, predictions_loop[[i]][[pred_string]])
  youden.threshold <- coords(my_roc, x="best", best.method="youden", ret = "threshold")[[1]]
  ci.auc <- ci.auc(my_roc)
  ci.auc.text <- paste("AUC CI: ", round(ci.auc[1],2), "-",round(ci.auc[3],2), " DeLong" , sep = "")
  ci.auc.texts <- append(ci.auc.texts, paste("AUC CI: ", round(ci.auc[1],2), "-",round(ci.auc[3],2), " DeLong" , sep = ""))
  # threshold for spec & sens
  predictions_loop[[i]] <- predictions_loop[[i]] %>% 
    mutate(.pred_class_youden = ifelse(predictions[[pred_string]] <= youden.threshold, "control", params$disease ),
           .pred_class_youden = factor(.pred_class_youden, levels = levels(predictions_loop[[i]]$disease))
    )
  
  #conf_mat_list[[i]] <- predictions_loop[[i]] %>%
  #  conf_mat(disease, .pred_class)
  
  # print(conf_mat_list[[i]])
  
  # CARET CONF MATRIX
  caret_conf_mat[[i]] <-  caret::confusionMatrix(predictions_loop[[i]]$.pred_class_youden, 
                                                 predictions_loop[[i]]$disease, 
                                                 positive = params$disease)
  print(caret_conf_mat[[i]])
  sensitiv <- append(sensitiv, caret_conf_mat[[i]][[4]][1])
  specific <- append(specific, caret_conf_mat[[i]][[4]][2])
  ppv <- append(ppv, caret_conf_mat[[i]][[4]][3])
  npv <- append(npv, caret_conf_mat[[i]][[4]][4])
  precision <- append(precision, caret_conf_mat[[i]][[4]][5])
  recall <- append(recall, caret_conf_mat[[i]][[4]][6])
  f1 <- append(f1, caret_conf_mat[[i]][[4]][7])
  
  # TEST ROC CURVE
  subtitle <- paste(wflow_id, " - Test set", sep = "")
  roc_plot_test <- predictions_loop[[i]] %>% 
      ## factor order usually alphabetically! (acs < control)
    mutate(disease = factor(disease, levels=c("control", params$disease))) %>%  
    roc_curve(disease, !!sym(pred_string), event_level="second") %>%
    ggplot(aes(1 - specificity, sensitivity)) +
    geom_line(linewidth = 1.5, color = ggthemes_data$few$colors$Dark[2,2][[1]]) +
    geom_abline(lty = 2, color = ggthemes_data$few$colors$Dark[1,2][[1]], size = 1.2, alpha=0.5) +
    geom_path(show.legend = FALSE) +
    coord_equal() +
    labs(title = paste0("ROC Curve (Predict ", text_disease, ")"),
         subtitle = subtitle) +
    annotate("text", x = 0.4, y=0.2, label = paste(wflow_id,"-AUC=", round(aucs[i],3), sep = ""), size=3, hjust = 0) +
    annotate("text", x = 0.4, y=0.15, label = paste(wflow_id, "-", ci.auc.texts[i], sep = ""), size=3, hjust = 0) +    
    ggthemes::theme_few()+
    ggthemes::scale_color_few()+
    theme(plot.subtitle = element_text(size = 7, color = "black"))
  print(roc_plot_test)
  
  ## factor order usually alphabetically! (acs < control)
  predictions_loop[[i]] <- predictions_loop[[i]] %>% 
    mutate(.pred_class_youden = factor(.pred_class_youden, levels=c("control", params$disease)),
           disease = factor(disease, levels=c("control", params$disease)),
           )   

  gbm::calibrate.plot(y = predictions_loop[[i]]$disease, p = predictions_loop[[i]][[pred_string]], 
                    main=paste(wflow_id, "-Calibration Plot", sep=""), 
                    line.par = list(col = "black"), shade.col="grey", xlim=c(0,0.6))
}
```

# Model Explanations

## Global Explanations

We compute variable importance by permutating features. If shuffling a column causes a large degradation in model performance, it is important and vica versa. This approach is model agnostic. 

```{r}
library(DALEXtra)
set.seed(20220908)
model_vars <- simple_rec %>% summary()
index <- #model_vars$variable != "id" &    # needed for global importance since in recipe
  model_vars$variable != "disease"

# modify data
predictor_vars <- model_vars[["variable"]][index]
vip_train <- dat_train %>% select(all_of(predictor_vars))

# create explainers | top model
fit1 <- extract_workflow(test_results1)
explainer1 <- 
  explain_tidymodels(
    fit1, 
    data = vip_train, 
    y = as.numeric(dat_train$disease), 
    label = topmodel1_race,
    verbose=FALSE
  )

fit2 <- extract_workflow(test_results2)
explainer2 <- 
  explain_tidymodels(
    fit2, 
    data = vip_train, 
    y = as.numeric(dat_train$disease), 
    label = topmodel2_race,
    verbose=FALSE
  )

# variable importance
vip1 <- model_parts(explainer = explainer1, 
            loss_function = loss_default("classification")    #  # loss_default(explainer_xgb$model_info$type) "One minus AUC"
            )
vip2 <- 
  model_parts(explainer = explainer2, 
            loss_function = loss_default("classification")    #  # loss_default(explainer_xgb$model_info$type) 
            )

filename.vip1.rds <- paste0("../output/dalextra/", format(params$date, "%Y%m%d"), "_",
                      params$disease,"_ANALYSIS_", params$analysis, "_vip1.rds")
filename.vip2.rds <- paste0("../output/dalextra/", format(params$date, "%Y%m%d"), "_",
                      params$disease,"_ANALYSIS_", params$analysis, "_vip2.rds")

saveRDS(vip1, file = filename.vip1.rds)
saveRDS(vip2, file = filename.vip2.rds)
```

```{r explain-global-func}
# custom TMwR plot function p 292
library(forcats)

ggplot_imp <- function(...) {
  obj <- list(...)
  metric_name <- attr(obj[[1]], "loss_name")
  metric_lab <- paste(metric_name, 
                      "after permutations\n(Global Feature Importance)")
  
  full_vip <- bind_rows(obj) %>%
    filter(variable != "_baseline_")
  
  perm_vals <- full_vip %>% 
    filter(variable == "_full_model_") %>% 
    group_by(label) %>% 
    summarise(dropout_loss = mean(dropout_loss))
  
  p <- full_vip %>%
    filter(variable != "_full_model_") %>% 
    mutate(variable = fct_reorder(variable, dropout_loss)) %>%
    ggplot(aes(dropout_loss, variable)) 
  if(length(obj) > 1) {
    p <- p + 
      facet_wrap(vars(label)) +
      geom_vline(data = perm_vals, aes(xintercept = dropout_loss, color = label),
                 size = 1.4, lty = 2, alpha = 0.7) +
      geom_boxplot(aes(color = label, fill = label), alpha = 0.2)
  } else {
    p <- p + 
      geom_vline(data = perm_vals, aes(xintercept = dropout_loss),
                 size = 1.4, lty = 2, alpha = 0.7) +
      geom_boxplot(fill = "#91CBD765", alpha = 0.4)
    
  }
  p +
    theme(legend.position = "none",
          axis.text.y = element_text(size=4)) +
    labs(x = metric_lab, 
         y = NULL,  fill = NULL,  color = NULL) +
    theme_few()
}
```


```{r plot-feature-importance-show, fig.height=17, fig.width=8}
ggplot_imp(vip1, vip2)
```
